doc.title: Ignacio Berroa interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 24, 2021 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Deciding at eleven to be a musician; violin and Nat King Cole
summary: His father brought home Nat King Cole and Glenn Miller albums; he was studying violin but heard the music he loved.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: That was early. That was early, during my childhood. I decided that I wanted to be a musician when I was eleven years old. When I was eleven years old my father came to our apartment with two albums, one by the Nat King Cole Trio and the second one was the Glenn Miller Orchestra with Gene Krupa on drums. By that time I was studying the violin, because my father used to play the violin and my mother wanted me to be like my dad. So I started fooling around with the violin and went to the National School of the Arts in Cuba to study violin. But I was never interested. I was never interested on the violin, and was afraid to tell my father because I didn’t want to hurt his feelings. My mom passed away when I was ten years old and I didn’t want to betray my mother and her memory. But anyway once I heard Nat King Cole one day something struck me, and something in my body told me I love that music. That’s the music I like.
Did you study Mozart and the European composers on the violin?
